analysis:
Both units are head_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 3157-3637). They contain historical release notes for already-recorded changes, not executable code, configuration or workflow files. The patch excerpt shows the only changed ranges are near the top of the file (head lines 11-39), adding a v0.10.10 candidate entry with waitlist gating, so the supplied excerpts are largely unchanged historical text and I found no changed security behavior in them.

The notes touch several threat-model topics: the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041, SEC-035), watchdog recovery (T-043), fan helper discovery (TB-010, T-046), staging and dev release lanes and the relaxed installer signature check for pre-release versions (T-034, T-054), App Attest worker and endpoint resumption (TB-011, T-053), and the per-environment keychain and cache namespaces. Since they are documentation only, they change no controls and do not contradict the threat model's 30-minute TTL or HMAC-keyed cache posture as far as the excerpts show.

One item the next pass should check against the actual workflow and script diffs, which are not in this batch, is the changelog's statement that installer scripts/install.sh relaxes the Apple-anchored signature requirement for versions containing -dev. or -staging. That is a release-environment tooling change. It is described as pinning the bundle identifier and keeping production strict, but this batch cannot confirm it. Whether a pre-release version string could be forged to reach the relaxed path depends on how the coordinator serves the installer and release metadata, which is outside the supplied evidence.

I do not report a finding because no source for that logic was supplied. The changelog text alone is not evidence of a regression, so I flag a low-confidence integration question.
